## What the agent can actually do

When you run an agent like Claude Code, Cursor, or similar with execution enabled, it can:

- Read and write any file your user account can
- Run any command your shell can run
- Install packages, including from arbitrary sources
- Make network requests on your behalf
- Use any credential it finds — SSH keys, API tokens, browser cookies

. . .

It is, in effect, a **shell user with your privileges**. Not a sandboxed code box.



## Three classes of risk{.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Mistakes**

The agent does what you asked, badly.

`rm` in the wrong directory. Force-pushes the wrong branch. Pip-installs into system Python.
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Misalignment**

The agent does something you didn't ask for.

"Helpfully" deletes files it considers obsolete. Refactors code you wanted left alone.
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
**Injection**

Something the agent reads tells it to do something bad.

A README in a cloned repo, a comment in a file, output from a web fetch — all are inputs the agent might treat as instructions.
:::
:::

. . .

The first two are familiar. The third is new and underappreciated.

## What you should worry about, in order

1. **Credentials on disk.** SSH keys, `.env` files, cloud credentials, browser cookies. Anything in a dotfile.
2. **Files outside the project directory.** `~/Documents`, `~/Desktop`, the entire home directory.
3. **Networked side effects.** Pushes, deploys, API calls that cost money or send email.
4. **The project itself.** Less critical because you have version control. Right?

. . .

The risk ranking is roughly: *credentials > unrelated files > external systems > your code*.



## Defenses you can adopt{.smaller}

| Defense | Cost | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| Run the agent from a project directory, not `~` | None | Most "wrong file" mistakes |
| Commit before every agent session | None | Reverts bad edits |
| Keep secrets out of the project (`.env` in `.gitignore`) | None | Most credential leaks |
| Review diffs before accepting | Minutes | Misalignment |
| Disable auto-execution for shell commands | Friction | Injected/destructive commands |
| Use a separate user account or VM for risky work | Setup time | Catastrophic outcomes |

. . .

## Sandboxing: contain the blast radius{.smaller}

A sandbox is a restricted environment where the agent can run, but cannot reach:

- Files outside the sandbox (your home directory, SSH keys, other projects)
- Your real credentials (cloud, GitHub, email)
- Persistent state (a fresh sandbox starts clean every time)



## Common options, in increasing strength{.smaller}

| Option | Setup effort | Isolation |
|---|---|---|
| Separate Linux user account | Low | File system only |
| Docker / Podman container | Medium | File system + network + processes |
| Apptainer / Singularity | Medium | Same, oriented to HPC |
| Virtual machine (VM) | High | Full OS isolation |
| Cloud dev environment (Codespaces, devcontainers) | Low–medium | Full isolation, off your laptop |
